concept.title: People with disabilities
concept.shortdesc: People with sensory, physical, learning or neurodevelopmental disabilities or impairments, including children with special educational needs, and those described broadly as having a disability.

conbody.note: Draft group. Groups are a convenience for browsing the draft: the hierarchy was proposed by a second clustering pass and named by a language model, and no person has reviewed it.

ul.li: : Blind, partially sighted or visually impaired people of any age, including those with dual sight and hearing loss, and their parents.
: Deaf people, people with hearing loss, and hearing aid wearers.
: Autistic children, young people and adults, including those with Asperger's, and their families.
: People described broadly as having a disability, long-term health condition or mix of physical, mental and cognitive conditions.
: People who find it hard to move around because of age, illness or disability, without necessarily using a wheelchair.
: People who are neurodivergent, including ADHD, autism, dyslexia and other learning or sensory processing differences, especially children and young people.
: Open to people of any age combined with any ability, level or background, with no one targeted.
: Disabled adults, including those with physical, learning or profound and multiple disabilities, and some groups that also include children.
: Adults and young adults with a learning disability or learning difficulty, including dyslexia.
: Children and young people up to 25 who have special educational needs or disabilities, including those needing communication aids or extra support at school.
